incidente.resumo: On January 24, 2017 the primary SQL Server (NY-SQL02) triggered a bugcheck on the SQL Server process; the Stack Exchange network went read-only for about 5 minutes and then offline for 12 minutes because application-level failovers were disabled by a bug. Why the bugcheck occurred is unknown, though logs indicate a potential bad DIMM. Restarting the SQL service on NY-SQL02 brought the network back read-only, and read-write mode was restored after a sanity check.

descricao.texto: System degradation (read-only mode) starting at 17:53 UTC was noticed within 2 minutes; the text does not say how.
trechos: On January 24, 2017 starting at 17:53 UTC, we experienced system degradation (read only) followed by a site outage.
It took us 2 minutes to notice the issue, 5 minutes to locate the source of the issue and 10 minutes to get service restored.

descricao.texto: The primary SQL Server (NY-SQL02) triggered a bugcheck on the SQL Server process, initially putting it into a read-only state. Why the bugcheck happened is not known; logs indicate a potential bad DIMM.
trechos: The cause of the issue was our primary SQL Server (NY-SQL02) triggering a bugcheck on the SQL Server process.
This initially put the SQL server into a read-only state.
Currently we do not know why SQL Server caused a bugcheck, however logs indicate a potential bad DIMM.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: Automatic SQL Server failovers are not permitted; application-level logic is meant to keep sites online by querying standby servers read-only, but due to a bug application-level failovers were disabled, so the network went offline completely when the primary failed.
trechos: We do not permit automatic SQL Server failovers, instead opting for application-level logic to keep the sites online by querying the standby SQL servers in read-only mode.
However, due to a bug, application-level failovers were disabled, so Stack Overflow and the rest of the Stack Exchange network went offline completely when the primary SQL server failed.

passos.texto: A restart of the SQL service on NY-SQL02 brought the network back online in read-only mode, without waiting for the memory dump to complete.
trechos: A restart of the SQL service on NY-SQL02 brought the network back online in read only mode.
At our memory capacity (384GB), we opted to bring the network online rather than waiting for the memory dump to complete.

passos.texto: After a sanity check on SQL health, the sites were put back into read-write mode.
trechos: Once a sanity check on the SQL health was done, the sites were put back into read-write mode.

acoes.texto: Already done: NY-SQL02 was taken out of production for testing, including a memory test; NY-SQL01 handles all normal load.
trechos: We have since taken NY-SQL02 out of production and have it down for testing (including a memory test).
All of the normal load is being handled by NY-SQL01.

acoes.texto: Already done: the SQL cluster was brought up to 2016 SP1 CU1.
trechos: We also took this opportunity to bring this SQL cluster up to 2016 SP1 CU1.
The Stack Exchange network went into read-only mode for approximately 5 minutes before being offline for 12 minutes.

perguntas_em_aberto: Why SQL Server caused a bugcheck is not known; logs indicate a potential bad DIMM, and NY-SQL02 is down for testing including a memory test.

observacoes: Duration is the stated read-only period (about 5 minutes) plus the offline period (12 minutes); the text also says it took 2 minutes to notice, 5 to locate the source and 10 to restore service. Approximately 3.5 seconds of data may have been lost as uncommitted transactions were rolled back. dominio, categoria_causa and causa_raiz.status follow the stated failure (a SQL Server bugcheck); the possible bad DIMM is only indicated by logs and stays an open question.
